key_insight: A configurable chemical validity operator turns heuristic oxidation-state rules into a tunable prior that filters and guides generative materials discovery toward chemically plausible compositions.
engineering_relevance: This gives materials-design pipelines a practical control knob for balancing exploration versus chemical realism, improving the reliability of ultra-high-throughput screening and generation.
method: Built on SMACT to evaluate compositions using a data-informed oxidation-state model.
Exposes tunable thresholds so users can shift from permissive to conservative chemical constraints.
Can be used both as a screening filter and as a reinforcement-learning reward for generative models.
evidence_signal: Benchmarking six inorganic-crystal generative models showed they often reproduce stoichiometry but under-represent realistic oxidation-state combinations; the filter removed compositions relying on rarely observed oxidation states while retaining low-energy compounds near the convex hull.
watch_item: Because the operator depends on heuristic and data-informed oxidation-state assumptions, overly strict settings may reject novel but potentially valid candidates.
paper_title: Chemical filters for ultra-high-throughput materials screening and generation
